points.point: The Vault's signaling / non-signaling tester category is defined for cellular and WLAN device testing: CMX500 for R&D signaling, CMP180 for production non-signaling RF, where non-signaling mode is used to save test time.
points.label: partial
points.why: Mentions non-signaling RF vs signaling protocol, but omits cellular/WLAN framing, CMX500/CMP180 roles, and saving test time.

points.point: The Vault's tooling map assigns signaling/protocol testing to CMX500/CMW500 and production non-signaling to CMP180/CMP200/CMW100 — no radar role is assigned to these testers.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: Does not give the tooling map and implies radar-driven roles/capability impacts for testers, whereas reference says no radar role is assigned.

points.point: Radar measurement/stimulus needs in the Vault are served by a separate product class — the AREG800A automotive radar echo generator, not by a signaling or non-signaling tester.
points.label: partial
points.why: Mentions AREG800A radar capabilities, but does not clearly state radar needs are served by a separate product class, not signaling/non-signaling testers.

points.point: Radar-specific capability metrics in the Vault are radar-domain parameters (digital channels, objects per channel, instantaneous bandwidth, object range), unrelated to signaling-tester measurement lists.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: Lists radar-domain metrics but treats them as tester capability impacts, while reference says they are unrelated to signaling-tester measurement lists.

points.point: Radar signal scenario generation for module, receiver and DFS tests is attributed to the SMW200A vector signal generator, i.e. a generator rather than a signaling/non-signaling tester.
points.label: missing
points.why: No mention of SMW200A/vector signal generator for radar scenarios or DFS tests.

points.point: The single documented radar-related capability on a non-signaling tester is the CMP180 DFS waveform-playing option R&S CMP-KD359 for WLAN.
points.label: missing
points.why: No mention of CMP180 DFS waveform-playing option R&S CMP-KD359.

points.point: The only radar/communications convergence trend recorded is 6G MFSS/ISAC with a possible joint communications + radar sensing waveform.
points.label: partial
points.why: Mentions ISAC integrating sensing with communications, but not MFSS or that this is the only recorded convergence trend.

points.point: For ISAC the Vault lists only technical challenges (high bandwidth, radar equation, power density, spectrum coexistence, waveform design) and derives no tester measurement requirement from them.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: Lists ISAC challenges but derives tester requirements from them, while reference says the Vault derives none.

invented: Non-signaling tester capability is affected mainly on the RF side, while signaling tester capability is affected mainly on the protocol side
Higher radar frequencies and wider bandwidths push the tester toward higher RF/mmWave frequency coverage and wider instantaneous bandwidth
Beamforming, MIMO, and OTA radar/communication architectures push the tester toward OTA, multi-antenna, and chamber-based measurement capability
If radar capability is integrated with communications, the tester must also handle sensing-related waveform, coexistence, bandwidth, and power-density issues
